name: The drain that holds
about: The first story box: a roadside riparian trial, street drains that let leaves and water pool for the roots and still stop the flood, read by a sensor on the mesh. Every fact is checked against its source before it ships.

cover.subject: a kerb grate over a planted pit, roots reaching below it, the street above, after rain

headline.text: What falls on the street runs to the creek.

i-catch.things: a flooded gutter after the storm
a dry creek a street away
fill.i-catch.intention: Street drains that hold water for the roots, and still stop the flood.

w-draw.fact: Stormwater carries the street into the creek.
Hard ground sends the rain away fast.
Sponge cities and leaky weirs slow water down and let it soak in.

fill.i-dial.future: A kerb that drinks: leaves and water pool in a planted pit under the grate, and spill to the pipe only when it is full.

fill.s-craft.thing: A trial on one street: three grates over planted pits, a water-level and soil sensor on a mesh node, a printed sign at each.

h-strings.who: the council's drains team: the three pits
the creek's own committee: the plants
a café's printer: each week's readings slip
a neighbour for each grate: the leaves
